messages:
elena: Quick follow-up to the all-hands conversation about strategy. Opening this live thread for sharp questions about mission, market positioning, competitors, and any roadmap clarifications. Ill answer succinctly here. :sparkles:

javi: Is our mission still "developer-first" or are we moving toward a hybrid identity publicly? Trying to keep docs aligned.

elena: Developer-first remains primary. Public messaging emphasizes dev DX + predictable economics. Were explicit that Redwood is enterprise-ready, but thats an overlay not a pivot.

amanda: For sales calls, what's the two-sentence soundbite we can use vs cloud provider endpoints?

elena: "Redwood gives you the same API and runtime from prototyping to production, with cost controls and SLO-grade reliability built in." Short and repeatable.

kyle: Competitor note: how do we explain the value vs DIY OSS runtimes that tout low inference cost?

elena: Be honest: open runtimes can be cheaper at peak, but total cost of ownership and time-to-prod are often higher. We sell predictable costs, observability, and fallback behavior that keep apps live.

ajavi: (typo) meant raj earlier :) Are we changing our go-to-market to chase enterprise ARR faster?

elena: No wholesale change. PLG-led motion stays. Well add targeted enterprise motions where customers need contracts, private deployments, or compliance.

amanda: Roadmap: autoscaling vs multimodal — which is immediate? Customers keep asking about multimodal PoCs.

elena: Immediate infra work (autoscaling, cache diagnostics) because it reduces latency/cost and helps many customers now. Multimodal is exploratory and gated by our reliability bar.

kyle: Pricing question: any imminent changes to hosted billing models? Team wants clear guidance for quoting.

elena: Hosted stays per-token for now. Were formalizing committed-capacity plans and discounts for Dedicated and enterprise engagements.

security-bot: FYI: new SOC2 checklist doc uploaded to vault (link: https://vault.internal/soc2).

amanda: Could leadership publish a concise FAQ and a single slide with the top 4 talking points for sales?

elena: Yes  Ill coordinate with Product Marketing and Matt to produce a 1-page FAQ + one-slide bullets by EOD tomorrow and post it here.

kyle: One last quick: when evaluating open models for our catalog, what's the absolute deal-breaker?
\elena: Licenses that forbid commercial use or models that fail our performance/quality checks on representative prompts. License and infra performance are hard stops.

elena: Thanks all  short thread. If anyone needs a deeper sync, DM me and well set 15m. :rocket:
